authority: Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trademarks (CGPDTM), Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade, Ministry of Commerce and Industry

description.en: Registration of trademarks including brand names, logos, slogans, and other distinctive marks under the Trade Marks Act, 1999. A registered trademark provides the owner exclusive right to use the mark in connection with the goods or services for which it is registered.

verifiedConditions.claim: The trademark must be distinctive and capable of distinguishing the goods or services of one person from those of others. Marks that are generic, descriptive, or deceptive cannot be registered.

The trademark must not contain marks prohibited under Section 9 and Section 11 of the Trade Marks Act, including national emblems, official hallmarks, or marks identical or similar to existing registered trademarks.

unverifiedEligibility: Any person claiming to be the proprietor of a trademark used or proposed to be used can apply for registration.
Both individuals, partnership firms, companies, LLPs, trusts, and joint applicants can apply.
Foreign nationals and entities can apply through an agent with an address for service in India.
Convention applications from Paris Convention countries have priority filing benefits.

requirements.claim: Trademark application in Form TM-A with complete details of the applicant, trademark representation, and specification of goods/services is required.
A clear representation of the trademark is required. For word marks, the exact wording; for device marks, a digital image of the logo/design in prescribed format.
Specification of goods or services and the class(es) under the Nice Classification (45 classes) for which the trademark is to be registered.
Complete details of the applicant including name, address, nationality, and type of entity (individual, company, partnership, etc.).
Power of attorney (Form TM-48) is required if the application is filed through a trademark agent or attorney.
For convention applications claiming priority from a Paris Convention country, a certified copy of the priority document must be filed within 3 months.
If claiming prior use of the trademark, an affidavit of use with supporting evidence (invoices, advertisements) may strengthen the application.

processInformation.claim: Conduct a trademark search on the IP India portal to check if an identical or similar mark is already registered or pending in the same class.
File Form TM-A online through the IP India e-filing portal or physically at the appropriate Trademark Registry office (Mumbai, Delhi, Kolkata, Chennai, or Ahmedabad) based on the applicant's address.
The Trademark Examiner examines the application for compliance with the Trade Marks Act. An examination report is issued, which may accept the mark or raise objections.
If objections are raised, the applicant must respond within 30 days (extendable). A hearing may be requested if objections are not resolved through written response.
Upon acceptance, the trademark is published in the Trademark Journal for a period of 4 months, during which any person may oppose the registration by filing a notice of opposition.

processInformation.appliesTo: All trademark applications with no opposition or resolved opposition
processInformation.claim: If no opposition is filed within the 4-month period, or if opposition is decided in favor of the applicant, the trademark is registered and the registration certificate is issued.

output.claim: A Trademark Registration Certificate is issued containing the trademark number, registration date, proprietor details, class(es), and goods/services. Registration is valid for 10 years from the date of filing and can be renewed indefinitely for successive 10-year periods.

fees.applicability: E-filing of Form TM-A by individual, startup, or small enterprise (per class)
fees.claim: The government fee for e-filing a trademark application by an individual, startup, or small enterprise is Rs. 4,500 per class.

fees.applicability: E-filing of Form TM-A by other entities (company, LLP, etc.) per class
fees.claim: The government fee for e-filing a trademark application by entities other than individuals/startups/small enterprises is Rs. 9,000 per class.

fees.applicability: Physical filing of Form TM-A by individual, startup, or small enterprise (per class)
fees.claim: The government fee for physical filing of a trademark application by an individual, startup, or small enterprise is Rs. 5,000 per class.

fees.applicability: Physical filing of Form TM-A by other entities per class
fees.claim: The government fee for physical filing of a trademark application by entities other than individuals/startups/small enterprises is Rs. 10,000 per class.

processingTime.applicability: Complete trademark registration process from filing to registration (assuming no opposition)
processingTime.claim: The complete trademark registration process typically takes 18 to 24 months from filing to registration, including examination (1-3 months), publication period (4 months), and final registration. Contested applications may take significantly longer.

sources.title: IP India — Trademark Registration Portal
sources.publisher: Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trademarks, Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade, Government of India
sources.evidenceExcerpt: The IP India portal provides the official e-filing facility for trademark applications, fee schedule, trademark search, and status tracking. Form TM-A is the prescribed application form.
claimsSupported: Trademark applications are filed using Form TM-A through the e-filing portal or physical submission.
E-filing fees: Rs. 4,500 for individuals/startups/SMEs and Rs. 9,000 for others per class.
Physical filing fees: Rs. 5,000 for individuals/startups/SMEs and Rs. 10,000 for others per class.
Five Trademark Registry offices process applications based on applicant address.
Trademark search facility is available on the portal.
sources.uncertainty: Fee schedules may be updated by government notification. Processing timelines depend on examiner workload and potential objections.

sources.title: The Trade Marks Act, 1999
sources.evidenceExcerpt: The Trade Marks Act, 1999 governs the registration and protection of trademarks in India. Section 9 lists absolute grounds for refusal. Section 11 lists relative grounds. Section 18 prescribes the application procedure. Section 25 provides for 10-year registration with indefinite renewal.
claimsSupported: Any person claiming to be proprietor of a trademark can apply for registration.
Marks must be distinctive and not fall under prohibited categories.
Publication in Trademark Journal for 4 months allows opposition.
Registration is valid for 10 years and can be renewed indefinitely.
Opposition period of 4 months from publication date.
sources.uncertainty: The Act has been amended and rules updated; specific procedural timelines may vary.

limitations: This record covers new trademark registration only, not renewal, assignment, transmission, or licensing.
Multi-class applications and their fee implications are simplified; each class requires a separate fee.
The opposition procedure and contested proceedings are outlined but not fully modeled.
Geographical indications, collective marks, and certification marks have separate procedures not covered here.
International trademark registration under the Madrid Protocol is not covered.
Professional agent fees for trademark filing are not established as they vary widely.

review.reviewReason: Core registration process and fee structure are reviewed, but opposition proceedings, international filings, and special mark types remain unmodeled.
nextReviewTrigger: Updates to the Trade Marks Rules affecting fees or procedures.
Changes to the IP India e-filing portal or application process.
Amendments to the Trade Marks Act, 1999.
New categories of marks or classification changes.
